items.description: Analyze repository structure, tooling, and agent capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/repo_analysis.md documenting: (a) all modules and their purposes, (b) available tools (concept_evolve commands: evolve/probe/reframe/walk; semantic_scholar commands: search/citations/references/recommend/graph/bibtex), (c) agent permission matrix from .archivara/opencode.json, (d) planned output directory structure under results/

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature search on univalent Bloch constant bounds using web search and Semantic Scholar
items.acceptance_criteria: Search Semantic Scholar and web for: (1) 'univalent Bloch constant', (2) 'Bloch-Landau constant extremal', (3) 'Skinner univalent Bloch 2009', (4) 'Carroll Ortega-Cerda harmonic symmetry', (5) 'Beller Hummel univalent Bloch 1985', (6) 'Goodman Bloch-Landau schlicht 1945', (7) 'Yanagihara locally univalent Bloch', (8) 'Bonk Bloch constant improvement'. Collect at least 15 distinct relevant papers. Record all results in results/phase1/literature_search_log.json with query, source, and findings per entry

items.description: Create and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: File sources.bib exists at repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 15 relevant papers including: Skinner2009, Yan1995, BS2023, BellerHummel1985, Carroll2008extension, CarrollOrtegaCerda2008, Goodman1945, ChenShiba2004, Bonk1990, ChenGauthier1996, Xiong1998, AhlforsGrunsky1937, Rademacher1943, Minda1982, and at least one additional source. Each entry must have author, title, journal/venue, year, and DOI or URL where available

items.description: Deep-dive analysis of Skinner's 2009 method yielding B_u > 0.5708858 (current best lower bound)
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/skinner_method_analysis.md containing: (a) precise statement of Skinner's theorem and proof strategy, (b) the role of Koebe-type distortion theorems for univalent functions, (c) identification of where the bound is loose and which inequalities contribute most to the gap, (d) comparison with Beller-Hummel 1985 approach, (e) at least 3 specific mathematical bottlenecks preventing tighter bounds. Must cite [Skin2009] and [BellerHummel1985] from sources.bib

items.description: Analyze upper bound landscape: Carroll-Ortega-Cerda construction and Goodman domains
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/upper_bound_analysis.md covering: (a) the Goodman 1945 domain construction for upper bounds on B_u, (b) Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's 2008 improved upper bound using harmonic symmetry and conformal welding, (c) the Polya-Chebotarev problem connection, (d) the exact known upper bound value, (e) gap analysis between best lower (0.5708858) and best upper bounds. Must reference at least 4 papers from sources.bib

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to mine citation graphs for cross-domain transferable techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner subagent with seed papers: Skinner2009 (paperId 4e70e76bcdcc5570677677ce2c4c5d333ce1ea09), CarrollOrtegaCerda2008 (paperId a3c98ff25aff7e3f41e18f5de916ee99b9f39693), BellerHummel1985 (paperId 84371d5da86c89636dc787980d5b61e405861816). Produce results/phase1/citation_graph_report.json with: (a) at least 30 papers in the 2-hop citation neighborhood, (b) identified cross-domain techniques from extremal problems, conformal mapping optimization, or computational complex analysis, (c) at least 5 actionable leads ranked by relevance

items.description: Implement numerical computation of B_f for specific univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/compute_Bf.py (Python with mpmath/numpy/scipy) that: (a) computes B_f for a given univalent f by discretizing the image domain and finding the largest univalent disk, (b) verifies B_f = 1 for the identity f(z) = z, (c) computes B_f for the Koebe function K(z) = z/(1-z)^2, (d) computes B_f for at least 3 other classical univalent functions (e.g., rotations of Koebe, z/(1-z), z-z^2/2). Output stored in results/phase2/baseline_Bf_values.json with function name, computed B_f, and precision estimate

items.description: Implement Skinner's lower bound argument computationally to reproduce B_u > 0.5708858
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/reproduce_skinner.py that numerically reproduces Skinner's argument: (a) implements the distortion-based lower bound chain, (b) outputs intermediate constants and inequalities used, (c) obtains a numerical value matching or exceeding 0.5708858. Store verification log in results/phase2/skinner_reproduction.json with step-by-step values. If exact reproduction is not possible (e.g., key technical lemma requires symbolic work), document precisely which steps succeed and which require further work

items.description: Implement conformal mapping toolkit for extremal domain exploration
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/conformal_toolkit.py providing: (a) Schwarz-Christoffel mapping for polygonal domains, (b) numerical conformal mapping of slit-disk domains (motivated by Goodman/Carroll-Ortega-Cerda), (c) computation of hyperbolic metric and Bloch radius in mapped domains, (d) unit tests verifying known values for simple domains. Toolkit must be importable by later phase scripts

items.description: Establish evaluation metrics and comparison framework against prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase2/metrics_framework.md and results/phase2/bounds_table.json documenting: (a) complete historical timeline of B_u bounds (lower and upper) with years and references from sources.bib, (b) definition of improvement metric: delta over best known bound and number of significant digits gained, (c) hierarchy of related constants B <= B_l <= L <= B_u with their best known values, (d) criteria for what constitutes a 'non-trivial' improvement (quantified)

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to identify missing methodological links
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse results/concept_evolve/tree/ (after item_015 populates it). Produce results/phase2/concept_gaps.json identifying: (a) at least 3 concept pairs that lack a connecting technique, (b) prioritized list of experimental concept paths to pursue in Phase 3, (c) mapping from concept paths to specific mathematical strategies for improving B_u bounds

items.description: Investigate variational approach: optimize over univalent functions to tighten lower bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/variational_lower_bound.py implementing: (a) parametrize univalent functions via truncated coefficient sequences (de Branges/Bieberbach constraints |a_n| <= n), (b) formulate B_f as an optimization problem, (c) use gradient-based or Bayesian optimization to search for the infimum of B_f over coefficient space, (d) report any candidate extremal function. Produce results/phase3/variational_results.json with: best candidate lower bound found, the extremal function coefficients (truncated), and comparison against 0.5708858

items.description: Investigate improved distortion estimates for univalent functions to sharpen Skinner-type bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/improved_distortion.py and results/phase3/improved_distortion_analysis.md: (a) implement sharper versions of Koebe distortion and growth theorems using higher-order coefficient information, (b) explore whether incorporating Fekete-Szego inequality or Grunsky coefficients yields tighter B_f estimates, (c) derive and verify numerically any improved inequality chain, (d) report new lower bound value (even if marginal improvement). Must cite relevant distortion theorem papers from sources.bib

items.description: Investigate upper bound via computational construction of near-extremal domains
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/upper_bound_search.py that: (a) parametrizes slit-disk domains (following Goodman/Carroll-Ortega-Cerda paradigm), (b) numerically optimizes slit configurations to minimize B_f while maintaining univalence, (c) explores harmonic symmetry constraints computationally, (d) reports best upper bound found with domain description. Produce results/phase3/upper_bound_results.json. If upper bound < 1 is achieved, compare with known upper bounds from literature

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve to generate cross-domain concept tree for the univalent Bloch constant problem
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve evolve with topic 'Improving bounds on the univalent Bloch constant B_u for schlicht functions: variational methods, extremal domain construction, conformal mapping optimization, distortion theorems, and computational complex analysis'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/index.json exists with at least 8 concept folders, each containing concept.json and README.md. Verify results/concept_evolve/semantic_bridge.json has nodes and edges. Verify results/concept_evolve/steering_directions.json has at least 3 directions

items.description: Explore hyperbolic geometry and Schwarz-Pick approach to lower bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/hyperbolic_approach.py and results/phase3/hyperbolic_approach.md: (a) reformulate B_u in terms of hyperbolic geometry of the image domain, (b) use Schwarz-Pick lemma and its generalizations to derive independent lower bound estimates, (c) explore whether the Beardon-Minda refinement of Schwarz-Pick or Rivard's sharp estimates yield non-trivial bounds on B_u, (d) compare with Skinner's bound. Must cite at least 2 papers from sources.bib

items.description: Investigate interval arithmetic / computer-assisted proof techniques for rigorous bound certification
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase3/rigorous_bounds.py using mpmath interval arithmetic: (a) implement key inequalities from the lower bound argument with guaranteed error bounds, (b) verify that any numerical improvement found in items 012-013 can be certified rigorously (i.e., all floating point errors accounted for), (c) produce a certificate file results/phase3/bound_certificate.json with the proven bound, method, and error analysis. If no improvement over 0.5708858 is achieved, document the tightest rigorous bound obtained and the specific obstacles

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to find techniques from adjacent extremal problems (capacity, transfinite diameter, Robin constant)
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner subagent with queries focused on: (a) Polya-Chebotarev problem and extremal domains, (b) logarithmic capacity and transfinite diameter in conformal mapping, (c) Robin constant optimization for simply connected domains, (d) computational methods for Schwarz-Christoffel parameters. Produce results/phase3/adjacent_techniques_report.json with at least 5 techniques potentially transferable to the B_u problem, each with: source paper, technique description, and hypothesized application to B_u

items.description: Systematic numerical experiment: sweep over parametric families of univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/parametric_sweep.py that: (a) defines at least 5 parametric families of univalent functions (Koebe rotations, convex combinations, starlike functions with parameters, close-to-convex families, bounded turning functions), (b) computes B_f for each function on a dense parameter grid (at least 1000 points per family), (c) identifies the minimum B_f found and the corresponding function, (d) produces results/phase4/parametric_sweep_results.json and at least one visualization in figures/. Compare the infimum found against B_u > 0.5708858

items.description: Evaluate all novel approaches against the baseline 0.5708858 bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/evaluation_summary.json consolidating results from items 012, 013, 014, 016, 017, and 019: (a) table of all bounds obtained (lower and upper) with method name, value, and whether rigorously certified, (b) identification of the single best new lower bound and single best new upper bound, (c) comparison against the prior art table from item_010, (d) statistical analysis of computational experiments (convergence, sensitivity to parameters)

items.description: Ablation study: identify which components of the best approach contribute most to improvement
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase4/ablation_study.md and results/phase4/ablation_data.json: (a) for the best-performing approach, systematically disable or simplify components, (b) measure the impact of each component on the final bound, (c) identify the critical mathematical insight (if any) that drives the improvement, (d) assess whether the improvement generalizes or is specific to a particular function family

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to evaluate concept paths against experimental results
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer subagent with the populated concept tree from item_015 and experimental results from items 019-021. Produce results/phase4/concept_evaluation.json rating each concept path by: (a) whether it led to a concrete bound improvement, (b) unexplored but promising directions, (c) dead ends to document. At least 3 concept paths must be evaluated with quantitative outcomes

items.description: Attempt to construct explicit near-extremal univalent function witnessing the upper bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/extremal_construction.py that: (a) uses insights from items 014 and 019 to construct the best candidate extremal function (one minimizing B_f), (b) verifies univalence rigorously (via e.g. checking |f'(z)| > 0 and injectivity on a fine grid, or Noshiro-Warschawski theorem), (c) computes B_f with certified accuracy, (d) produces results/phase4/extremal_function.json with coefficient representation and computed B_f value. This gives a concrete new upper bound for B_u

items.description: Synthesize all results into a coherent mathematical narrative with rigorous statements
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/main_results.md containing: (a) precise statement of any new bounds obtained (both lower and upper), (b) complete proof or proof sketch for any claimed improvement, (c) comparison table against all prior work from sources.bib, (d) discussion of the tightness of the new bounds and remaining gap, (e) at least 5 citations from sources.bib. If no strict improvement over 0.5708858 is achieved, document the best bound obtained, the obstacles encountered, and concrete strategies for future work

items.description: Document all negative results and failed approaches with analysis of why they failed
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/negative_results.md documenting: (a) every approach attempted that did not yield improvement, (b) specific mathematical reason for failure in each case, (c) whether the failure reveals structural constraints on the problem, (d) lessons learned for future researchers. Must cover at least 3 distinct approaches

items.description: Produce final bounds summary and update the constant description
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/final_bounds.json with: (a) best lower bound achieved (value, method, rigorously certified: yes/no), (b) best upper bound achieved (value, method, witnessing function if applicable), (c) delta improvement over prior art (0.5708858 for lower, 1.0 for upper), (d) confidence assessment. Also produce results/phase5/updated_constant_card.md reformatting the constant description with any new bounds added to the tables

items.description: Generate visualizations of key results and the bound landscape
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce at least 3 figures in figures/: (a) figures/bounds_timeline.png — historical timeline of B_u bounds with any new bounds marked, (b) figures/extremal_domain.png — visualization of the best near-extremal domain found, (c) figures/parametric_landscape.png — heatmap or contour plot of B_f over the parameter space explored. Each figure must have title, axis labels, and legend

items.description: Final peer review pass: verify all claims, check citations, validate code outputs
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/review_report.md with: (a) verification that all numerical claims match code outputs, (b) check that all citations in sources.bib are actually referenced in result documents, (c) verification that any claimed rigorous bound has a valid certificate, (d) list of any remaining open questions or caveats, (e) sign-off on reproducibility (all scripts runnable with documented dependencies). Review must explicitly address whether any new non-trivial bound was achieved and if not, what the closest approach was
